2  JUDGMENT
This appeal has been filed by the second respondent insurer in OP(MV) No.559 of 2002 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Attingal.
The respondents 1 to 3 herein were the claimants and respondents 4 to 14 herein were respondents 1, 3 to 6 & 8 to 13 before the tribunal.

2. Before the tribunal, the case of the claimants was that on 10.03.2002, while the deceased was pillion riding along with her parents on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-01/P-3741, a car bearing Reg.No.KRA-8638 driven by the fourth respondent knocked them down, whereby she sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The claimants, being the legal heirs of the deceased,
approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 2,49,500/-.
3. Respondents 2, 3, 6 and 10 to 13 appeared before the tribunal and filed written statements.

The respondent insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy coverage for the offending vehicle,
but disputing the liability on the ground that the policy was 'act only policy' and quantum of compensation claimed.

Before the tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A21 were marked on the side of the 2025:KER:39996 ..4..
claimants and Ext.B1 on the side of the respondents.
The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 1,52,500/- as compensation under different heads.

Further,
finding that the accident took place on account of negligence on the part of the drivers of both vehicles, the tribunal allowed the claimants to realize 50% of the compensation awarded from the second respondent insurer of the motorcycle, and the remaining 50% from respondents 3 & 4, who are the owner and driver of the car.

The second respondent insurer has come up in appeal,
challenging the finding of the tribunal that the claimants are entitled to realize from them 50% of the compensation awarded.

4. Heard the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/second respondent insurer and the learned counsel for the fourth respondent/owner of the motorcycle.
5.
The learned Standing Counsel for the appellant insurer submits that the policy in respect of the motorcycle was an 'act only' policy and hence, the insurer is not liable to pay compensation.
I find force in the submission of the learned Standing Counsel.

This court in New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
v. Daisy Paul & another [2021 (2) KHC 449], has held that when the policy is an act only policy, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the amount.

Accordingly, I hold 2025:KER:39996 ..5..
that the policy being an 'act only' policy, the insurer cannot be held liable to pay the amount.
The claimants are entitled to realize the compensation amount from the owner of the vehicle.

sentences.text: "Thereafter, the petitioners filed E.P.No.75/2011 for realization of the award amount from the 2nd respondent, the insurance company.
An amount of Rs.129742/- was realized from the insurance company through attachment and the petitioners got released their respective shares.
For realization of the award amount from the 3rd respondent, the petitioners filed E.P No.65/2014.
An amount of Rs.88437/- was realized through revenue recovery proceedings from the 3rd respondent and E.P No.65/2014 was closed as satisfied on 09.02.2018.
The amount thus realized is currently kept in fixed deposit in this Tribunal.
However, the petitioners have not taken steps to release the amount kept in the fixed deposit till date.

With respect to the realization of the balance award amount from the 4th respondent,
the Counsel for the petitioners informed that a payment of Rs.65000/- was made by the 4th respondent to the petitioners through an out of Court settlement on 24.09.2013.

Thus the entire award amount has been realized from the respondents as per the award in OP(MV) No.559/2022 on the file of the Tribunal."
7.

From the above report, it is evident that the entire compensation has been realized from the appellant insurer as well as 2025:KER:39996 ..6..
from respondents 5 & 6, who are the owner and driver of the offending car.
However, as already held, since the policy in respect of the motorcycle was an 'act only' policy, the appellant insurer is not liable to pay compensation to the claimants.
Hence, I deem it appropriate to grant a right of recovery to the appellant insurer against the fourth respondent/owner of the motorcycle.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The appellant insurer is allowed to recover the amount already paid by them to the claimants, through attachment, from the fourth respondent/owner of the motorcycle.

SD/-
